sara: quick Q — trying to import an existing Route53 Resolver rule into our infra TF in prod (shared-services account owns it). `terraform plan` fails with duplicate resource name. Anyone done a clean import for cross-account resolver rules?

ben: can you paste the exact error and the resource block?

sara: error: "Error: creating Route53 Resolver Rule: DuplicateResource: Resolver rule with the same name already exists"
snippet of our resource:```hcl
resource "aws_route53_resolver_rule" "shared_privatelink" {
  domain_name = "internal.redwood-privatelink.example"
  rule_type  = "FORWARD"
  resolver_endpoint_id = aws_route53_resolver_endpoint.shared.id
  lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }
}
```

kai: two quick approaches: import the existing resolver rule into the state, or switch to a `data` block that references it (if you don't need to manage it here).

sara: tried `terraform import aws_route53_resolver_rule.shared_privatelink rslvr-0a1b2c3d4e5f` but TF still complains on plan because the `resolver_endpoint_id` differs (endpoint is in another account).

ben: for cross-account resolver rules the endpoint association is often the wrinkle. If shared-services manages the endpoint, we should `data` it instead. Example:```hcl
data "aws_route53_resolver_rule" "shared_privatelink" {
  id = "rslvr-0a1b2c3d4e5f"
}
``` then reference `data.aws_route53_resolver_rule.shared_privatelink.id` where needed. No import required.

kai: also check permissions — the account doing the import needs `route53resolver:GetResolverRule` and `AssociateResolverRule` on the VPC side. Cross-account imports sometimes succeed but plans show diffs because of missing associated VPCs.

sara: ok. We actually need to create a `aws_route53_resolver_rule_association` in our account so resolver rule gets associated to the app VPC. That requires the rule to allow association from another account (shared-services must have allowed associations).

ben: ping @netops-team to confirm they allowed cross-account associations and to share the rule id if they prefer we import vs consume as data.

netops-bot: Reminder: open a ticket with shared-services for rule association requests. Ticket template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/NETOPS-TEMPLATE

kai: if shared-services wants us to import, ask them to share the exact `resolver_endpoint_id` and association state. Otherwise use `data` + `aws_route53_resolver_rule_association` resource in our module. Example:```hcl
resource "aws_route53_resolver_rule_association" "app_assoc" {
  resolver_rule_id = data.aws_route53_resolver_rule.shared_privatelink.id
  vpc_id           = var.app_vpc_id
}
```

sara: will try switching to `data` + association and open a netops ticket. one more thing: the privatelink NLB uses an alias A record in the shared hosted zone, so we might also need `route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets` permissions when we update DNS.

ben: yep — coordinate DNS RBAC with shared-services. If you're doing an import path, also check TF provider version; older `hashicorp/aws` had differences around resolver rule import semantics. Use `>= 5.8.0` in the meantime.

sara: thanks. i'll attempt `data`+association and post the plan here. cc @kai for review. :thumbsup:
